# PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis — facts

## How it works

- [statement] The 2015 MDS criteria first require motor parkinsonism: bradykinesia together with rest tremor, rigidity, or both. Parkinsonism alone does not establish PD as its cause. (medium confidence) — https://www.med.upenn.edu/digitalneuropathologylab/assets/user-content/documents/educational-resources/mds-clinical-diagnostic-criteria-for-parkinson's-disease.pdf · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12748991/
- [statement] NICE NG71 recommends prompt, untreated referral to a specialist in differential diagnosis when PD is suspected, and regular diagnostic review at six- to twelve-month intervals with reconsideration if atypical features develop. Its diagnostic recommendation explicitly names the UK Brain Bank criteria. (low confidence) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] In the 2018 eight-centre validation cohort of 626 patients, probable MDS PD had 94.5% sensitivity, 88.5% specificity and 92.6% overall accuracy against expert clinical diagnosis. These estimates measure agreement with expert clinical diagnosis, not autopsy confirmation. (low confidence) — https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30145797/ · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] MDS red flags have explicit timing and severity: wheelchair-requiring gait progression within five years, severe autonomic failure within five years, and recurrent balance-related falls within three years; bilateral symmetric onset is another red flag. Confounding explanations and timing must be considered. (low confidence) — https://www.med.upenn.edu/digitalneuropathologylab/assets/user-content/documents/educational-resources/mds-clinical-diagnostic-criteria-for-parkinson's-disease.pdf · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] The 2015 MDS criteria were designed to codify expert clinical diagnosis for research and can guide clinical assessment; diagnostic accuracy varies with disease duration and examiner expertise, so criteria performance should not be treated as one universal accuracy number. (medium confidence) — https://www.med.upenn.edu/digitalneuropathologylab/assets/user-content/documents/educational-resources/mds-clinical-diagnostic-criteria-for-parkinson's-disease.pdf · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis · also: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30145797/
- [statement] A predominantly lower-limb gait syndrome can suggest vascular parkinsonism, but cerebrovascular imaging abnormalities are not conclusive because vascular disease and PD may coexist. Normal-pressure hydrocephalus is another potentially treatable mimic with gait, urinary and cognitive symptoms and ventriculomegaly. (low confidence) — https://exonpublications.com/index.php/exon/article/view/191/349 · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] The UK Parkinson’s Disease Society Brain Bank criteria, reproduced from Gibb and Lees (1988), first define a parkinsonian syndrome as bradykinesia plus at least one of muscular rigidity, 4–6 Hz rest tremor, or postural instability not caused by primary visual, vestibular, cerebellar or proprioceptive dysfunction (step 1); step 2 lists exclusion criteria for Parkinson’s disease, including supranuclear gaze palsy, cerebellar signs, early severe autonomic involvement and neuroleptic treatment at onset of symptoms. (low confidence) — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK379754/ · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] Step 3 of the UK Parkinson’s Disease Society Brain Bank criteria lists supportive prospective positive criteria, three or more of which are required for diagnosis of definite Parkinson’s disease: unilateral onset, rest tremor present, progressive disorder, persistent asymmetry affecting the side of onset most, excellent response (70–100%) to levodopa, severe levodopa-induced chorea, levodopa response for 5 years or more, and a clinical course of 10 years or more. (low confidence) — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK379754/ · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Asymmetric parkinsonism with higher cortical features such as apraxia, cortical sensory loss or alien-limb phenomena suggests corticobasal syndrome rather than typical PD. (low confidence) — https://exonpublications.com/index.php/exon/article/view/191/349 · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis

## Facts and statements

- [statement] MDS bradykinesia requires slowness plus decrement in amplitude or speed, or progressive hesitations/halts, during continued movement; limb bradykinesia must be documented. (low confidence) — https://www.med.upenn.edu/digitalneuropathologylab/assets/user-content/documents/educational-resources/mds-clinical-diagnostic-criteria-for-parkinson's-disease.pdf · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] Clinically established PD under the 2015 MDS criteria requires no absolute exclusion, at least two supportive criteria, and no red flags. Clinically probable PD permits at most two red flags, each counterbalanced by a supportive criterion, with no absolute exclusion. (medium confidence) — https://www.med.upenn.edu/digitalneuropathologylab/assets/user-content/documents/educational-resources/mds-clinical-diagnostic-criteria-for-parkinson's-disease.pdf · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12748991/
- [statement] Supportive MDS features include a clear and dramatic dopaminergic treatment response, levodopa-induced dyskinesia, and clinically documented limb rest tremor; merely some improvement on treatment does not satisfy the dramatic-response criterion. (low confidence) — https://www.med.upenn.edu/digitalneuropathologylab/assets/user-content/documents/educational-resources/mds-clinical-diagnostic-criteria-for-parkinson's-disease.pdf · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] Examples of 2015 MDS absolute exclusions are unequivocal cerebellar abnormalities, downward vertical supranuclear gaze palsy or selective slowing of downward saccades, and dopamine-blocking/depleting exposure whose dose and time course fit drug-induced parkinsonism. (low confidence) — https://www.med.upenn.edu/digitalneuropathologylab/assets/user-content/documents/educational-resources/mds-clinical-diagnostic-criteria-for-parkinson's-disease.pdf · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] Essential tremor commonly produces bilateral postural/action tremor; PD can also have postural/action tremor, so tremor appearance alone is insufficient for diagnosis. (low confidence) — https://exonpublications.com/index.php/exon/article/view/191/349 · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] Medication review is central to differential diagnosis: drug-induced parkinsonism can be symmetric but can also closely mimic PD; symptoms often resolve after withdrawal, while continued progression can reflect underlying PD unmasked by the drug. (low confidence) — https://exonpublications.com/index.php/exon/article/view/191/349 · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] Early prominent autonomic problems, cerebellar signs or stridor raise suspicion of multiple system atrophy; early falls with vertical eye-movement abnormalities raise suspicion of progressive supranuclear palsy. These are differential clues, not guarantees of pathology. (medium confidence) — https://exonpublications.com/index.php/exon/article/view/191/349 · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis · also: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12748991/
- [statement] Functional parkinsonism is assessed using positive examination signs such as effortful slowness without decrement, improvement with distraction, variable tremor, and active resistance during passive movement. (low confidence) — https://exonpublications.com/index.php/exon/article/view/191/349 · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] The autopsy-based scoping review by Fox and colleagues found that supportive features were more common in PD and exclusions/red flags more common in atypical disorders, but some atypical features also occurred in pathologically confirmed PD. Limited clinical documentation, retrospective application of precise definitions and co-pathology constrain interpretation. (low confidence) — https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12748991/ · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
- [statement] NICE guideline NG71 (published 19 July 2017) advises against acute levodopa and apomorphine challenge tests in the differential diagnosis of parkinsonian syndromes, and against objective smell testing in that setting except in the context of clinical trials. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-27) — https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng71/chapter/recommendations · keywords: PD diagnosis criteria and differential diagnosis
